newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita says has no specific debt plan.
newsitem.headline: Merita says has no specific debt plan.

text.p: Finnish banking group Merita Oy is following debt markets closely but does not plan specifically to replace its debt to the state with private debt, Merita spokesman Timo Nikinmaa said on Friday.
"We have a target for Tier 1 capital (seven percent) and are below that, so it is normal that we are checking our options," Nikinmaa told Reuters, adding this was normal balance sheet management.
He was commenting on a report in daily Helsingin Sanomat that Merita was planning to replace its debt to the state -- some 3.48 billion markka of preferred capital investments -- with private debt.
The government's capital injection stems from a banking crisis in Finland in the early 1990s, and analysts say it is cheap capital for Merita.

The interest rate on the capital certificates is 0.50 percentage points above the cost of one-year treasury notes now at 3.46 percent, the margin rising to 1.5 percentage points next year, and to 3.5 percentage points at the start of 2001.

Merita plans to repay its debt to the government by 2001 at the latest, and the 1.5 percentage point interest rate margin from the start of next year will bring the total to about five percent, which Nikinmaa said is "still not at all expensive".
